question: Aphelion occurs in early ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**July**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **laws of Johannes Kepler**, all planets in the Solar system have **elliptical orbits** with the Sun at one of the focal points. 
 
• Now due to this reason at times, Earth will be closer to the sun and at times it will drift far away from the sun.**​**
 
• Aphelion, in astronomy, is the point in the orbit of a planet, comet, or other body most distant from the Sun.
 
• When Earth is at its aphelion in early July, it is about 4,800,000 km (3,000,000 miles) farther from the Sun than when at its perihelion in early January. 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86539eebf140e1772c353d1f324f0872a0038dcfe710727344193af27cd71c1f.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **elliptical orbit **of the **earth around the sun** is the cause for **aphelion and perihelion. **
 
• Another cause for this perihelion and aphelion may be the 23.5-degree tilt of the axis of Earth. This tilt results in the changing of the seasons.
 
• Earth's Perihelion and Aphelion:__
 __
 
• The Earth is closest to the Sun, or at the Perihelion, about 2 weeks after the December Solstice, when it is winter in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• Conversely, the Earth is farthest away from the Sun, at the Aphelion point, 2 weeks after the June Solstice, when the Northern Hemisphere is enjoying warm summer months.
 
• Mathematicians and astronomers estimate that in the year 6430, over 4000 years from now, the timing of the Perihelion and the March Equinox will coincide. 
 
 
 
• Perigee and Apogee:__
 __
 
• Like the Earth's orbit around the Sun, the Moon's path around the Earth is elliptical. 
 
• The point in the Moon's orbit that is closest to the Earth is called the Perigee and the point farthest from the Earth is known as the Apogee.
 
• The terms are also sometimes used interchangeably with the Earth's Perihelion and Aphelion. 
 
 
 
• Perihelion:__ The Earth reaches its perihelion on January 3 every year at a distance of about 147 million km from the Sun.
